# openhands-nti

> Drop-in Neutral Trust Infrastructure (NTI) guardrail for the OpenHands agent
> framework. Intercepts every OpenHands tool action (bash, Python, file edits,
> browser/web, MCP, client tools), signs it with ML-DSA-87, and verifies it
> against a Merkle delegation chain before execution. Fail-closed.

## Install

    pip install openhands-nti
    pip install "openhands-nti[openhands]"

## One-line usage

    from openhands_nti import NTIGuardrail

    NTIGuardrail(
        agent_did="did:webvh:z6Mk...:agents.example.com",
        key_pair=key_pair,                 # ube_foundation.PqcKeyPair (ML-DSA-87)
        delegation_chain=delegation_chain,
    ).install()

    # ... run your OpenHands agent as usual ...

`install()` patches `openhands.sdk.tool.tool.ToolDefinition.__call__`, the single
method every tool call funnels through. `uninstall()` restores it. The guardrail
also works as a context manager.

## Public API

- `NTIGuardrail(agent_did, key_pair, delegation_chain, verification_method=None,
  engine=None, capability_overrides=None, capability_resolver=None,
  float_policy="round", float_digits=15, audit_path=None, on_block=None)`
- `NTIGuardrail.install()` / `.uninstall()` / `.authorize(tool, action)`
- `install_guardrail(**kwargs)` - build and install in one call
- `verify_receipt(receipt, public_key)` - verify a receipt signature
- `build_receipt(...)`, `parse_tagged_signature(tag)`, `format_tagged_signature(sig)`
- `canonical_json(value, float_policy=..., float_digits=...)`, `action_message(...)`
- `build_proof(chain, subject, capability)`, `verify_proof(chain, proof)`,
  `merkle_root(leaves)`, `leaf_hash(record)`, `node_hash(left, right)`
- `capability_for(tool_name, overrides=None, resolver=None)`,
  `DEFAULT_TOOL_CAPABILITIES`
- `AuditTrail(path=None)` with `.records` and `.incidents()`

## Behavior

For each action, in order, all fail-closed:

1. Map the tool name to an NTI capability.
2. Prove a delegation record granting that capability to the agent DID is
   included in the Merkle chain (RFC 6962, NTI domain separators).
3. Canonicalize and sign with ML-DSA-87 over
   `(request_id, actor, capability, action, input)`.
4. Ask the NTI TrustEngine for a verdict; anything but `Allow` blocks.
5. Run the original tool and attach the signed receipt as
   `observation.nti_receipt`.

Any failure raises `NTIBlocked`, records an incident, and prevents execution.

## Receipts

`ml_dsa_87_signature` uses the NTI tagged form `ml-dsa-87:{length}:{hex}`.
Signatures are raw ML-DSA-87 bytes, never DER-encoded ECDSA. The signing payload
is domain-separated (`nti-openhands-action-v1:`) and length-prefixed.

## Capability mapping (defaults)

- `bash`, `terminal`, `execute_bash` -> `shell.execute`
- `str_replace_editor`, `file_editor`, `apply_patch` -> `file.write`
- `browser`, `browser_use`, `fetch`, `web_search` -> `web.fetch`
- `think` -> `agent.think`, `finish` -> `agent.finish`, `task_tracker` -> `agent.plan`
- unknown tools -> `tool.<name>`

## Security

Fail-closed by design. ML-DSA-87 via `ube-foundation`. Canonicalization is a
security boundary; see SECURITY.md for the float-canonicalization hazard and the
`float_policy` controls.
